bibl.title: Comprehensive Analysis of Long-Range Connectivity from and to the Posterior Parietal Cortex of the Mouse

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: In this study, we summarized the quantitative long-range connectivity from and to the PPC by analyzing the Allen Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas data and confirmed key findings by both anterograde and retrograde neurotracers.

span.label: long-range connectivity of the mouse posterior parietal cortex
span.quote: Although many recent works have been performed with the mouse as a model system, a comprehensive understanding of long-range connectivity of the mouse PPC is scarce, preventing integrative interpretation of the rapidly accumulating functional data.

span.label: atlas-data-reanalysis-and-tract-tracing
span.quote: In this study, we conducted a detailed neuroanatomic and bioinformatic analysis of the Allen Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas data to summarize afferent and efferent connections to/from the PPC.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Absence of a direct visual-to-motor cortical route forces visual decision signals through PPC, so inactivating PPC impairs visual but not whisker-based decisions
span.quote: There is essentially no direct connection between VIS and MO (Wang et al. 2012) and the main indirect connection from VIS to MO is through the PPC (Zingg et al. 2014).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Reciprocal PPC-thalamic loops sustain persistent choice-selective firing during a delay
span.quote: The current study showed that the PPC has a strong reciprocality with LP, PO, and LD, suggesting the possibility that the reciprocal connectivity with thalamic nuclei may be a general connectivity motif that supports the persistent activity.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Tracing and axon-volume quantification disagree because one reports where cell bodies sit and the other where synapses land
span.quote: For instance, when L5 neurons receive inputs on their distal dendrites, an experimental approach will show L5, where cell bodies are located, whereas bioinformatic analysis will show L1, where the synapses occur.

span.label: The PPC is small and its anatomical borders are weakly agreed on in mouse, so injection targeting could be imprecise.
span.note: what this limits: every result reported for mouse PPC, and every join on that label: THE PPC IS A RELATIVELY SMALL BRAIN REGION WITH A WEAK CONSENSUS ON ANATOMICAL BORDERS IN THE MOUSE BRAIN
span.quote: This leaves a potential problem considering that the PPC is a relatively small brain region with a weak consensus on anatomical borders in the mouse brain.

span.label: Few injections were available per structure in the atlas dataset, giving incomplete regional coverage.
span.note: what this limits: the regional coverage of the atlas: A RELATIVELY LIMITED NUMBER OF INJECTIONS FOR EACH STRUCTURE ... CAN RESULT IN INCOMPLETE COVERAGE OF THE BRAIN REGIONS, WHICH MAY DISPLAY A HIGH LEVEL OF INTRAREGIONAL VARIABILITY
span.quote: First, a relatively limited number of injections for each structure in the connectivity dataset can result in incomplete coverage of the brain regions, which may display a high level of intraregional variability.

span.label: The quantified signal is axonal, not synaptic, so laminar projection patterns must be read cautiously.
span.note: what this limits: any synaptic reading of the projection patterns: THE DETECTED SIGNAL IS PRIMARILY BASED ON AXONAL STRUCTURE INSTEAD OF SYNAPTIC INPUTS PER SE
span.quote: However, detailed projection patterns need to be interpreted with care since the detected signal is primarily based on axonal structure instead of synaptic inputs per se.

span.label: The LD and LP injections did not fill those nuclei, so the apparent mouse-rat thalamic difference is not yet established.
span.note: what this limits: the apparent mouse-rat thalamic difference: AS LD AND LP INJECTIONS ... DID NOT FILL THE ENTIRE LD OR LP, THE COMPLETE REGIONAL INJECTIONS OR ADDITIONAL NONOVERLAPPING SUBREGIONAL TARGETING ... ARE REQUIRED TO DEMONSTRATE A TRUE SPECIES DIFFERENCE
span.quote: As LD and LP injections examined in this study did not fill the entire LD or LP, the complete regional injections or additional nonoverlapping subregional targeting of mouse LD and LP are required to demonstrate a true species difference.

span.label: Two ways of delineating the same region are reported not to match.
span.note: what this limits: any boundary assigned to mouse PPC: even with functional retinotopic mapping using intrinsic optical imaging, voltage-sensitive dyes or Ca2+ responses, the boundaries of VISa and VISrl were not clearly defined or mismatched with the architectonic definition
span.quote: However, it has been reported that even with functional retinotopic mapping by intrinsic optical imaging, using voltage-sensitive dyes or Ca2+ responses, the boundaries of VISa and VISrl were not clearly defined or mismatched with the architectonic definition of the PPC

span.label: Injection quality varies by structure because selection falls back through three tiers.
span.note: what this limits: any comparison of projection strengths between structures here: injections occupying over 90% of the primary structure were preferred, with fallback to 75-90% and then 50-75% where none passed
span.quote: For cortical areas, injections with the primary injection structure occupying over 90% of total injection volume (considered a very well positioned injection—tier 1) were selected. If no injection passed this criterion, then the injections with the next highest primary injection ratio (75–90%—tier 2) were selected, followed by tier 3 (50

span.label: A printed result is withdrawn as an artefact on evidence the paper does not show.
span.note: what this limits: the CA3 projection signal reported here: the authors state it appears to have resulted from a false positive quantification from the path through the ventral internal capsule
span.quote: The projection signal in CA3 appears to have resulted from a false positive quantification from the path through the ventral part of the internal capsule and then the cerebral peduncle

span.label: The threshold for showing a connection differs between structure classes.
span.note: what this limits: any connection matrix read from this paper: only connections above threshold are shown, and the threshold is not the same for cortical and thalamic structures
span.quote: Only strong connections above threshold (0.1 for cortical and 0.05 for thalamic structures) are shown in a color scale

span.label: functional retinotopic mapping
span.quote: However, it has been reported that even with functional retinotopic mapping by intrinsic optical imaging, using voltage-sensitive dyes or Ca2+ responses, the boundaries of VISa and VISrl were not clearly defined or mismatched with the architectonic definition of the PPC

span.label: architectonic definition
span.quote: However, it has been reported that even with functional retinotopic mapping by intrinsic optical imaging, using voltage-sensitive dyes or Ca2+ responses, the boundaries of VISa and VISrl were not clearly defined or mismatched with the architectonic definition of the PPC

span.label: primary injection structure
span.quote: For cortical areas, injections with the primary injection structure occupying over 90% of total injection volume (considered a very well positioned injection—tier 1) were selected. If no injection passed this criterion, then the injections with the next highest primary injection ratio (75–90%—tier 2) were selected, followed by tier 3 (50

span.label: false positive quantification
span.quote: The projection signal in CA3 appears to have resulted from a false positive quantification from the path through the ventral part of the internal capsule and then the cerebral peduncle

span.label: strong connections above threshold
span.quote: Only strong connections above threshold (0.1 for cortical and 0.05 for thalamic structures) are shown in a color scale

span.label: the PPC's borders - TWO DELINEATIONS THAT DISAGREE: there is a weak consensus on anatomical borders, and the paper reports that functional retinotopic mapping did not clearly define the boundaries or mismatched the architectonic definition, so the region has two methods of fixing it and they do not agree
span.quote: However, it has been reported that even with functional retinotopic mapping by intrinsic optical imaging, using voltage-sensitive dyes or Ca2+ responses, the boundaries of VISa and VISrl were not clearly defined or mismatched with the architectonic definition of the PPC

span.label: a selected injection - ONE OF THREE TIERS: preference is for injections occupying over 90% of the primary structure, falling back to 75-90% and then 50-75% where nothing passed, so the phrase 'representative injection' covers three grades of evidence and the result does not say which
span.quote: For cortical areas, injections with the primary injection structure occupying over 90% of total injection volume (considered a very well positioned injection—tier 1) were selected. If no injection passed this criterion, then the injections with the next highest primary injection ratio (75–90%—tier 2) were selected, followed by tier 3 (50

span.label: a false-positive attribution - A CORRECTION WITHOUT ITS EVIDENCE: a printed projection signal is attributed to quantification of a fibre path rather than a terminal field, and the reader is asked to discount the result on that basis
span.quote: The projection signal in CA3 appears to have resulted from a false positive quantification from the path through the ventral part of the internal capsule and then the cerebral peduncle

span.label: builds-on → Oh et al. 2014; Harris et al. 2019 (brain-wide quantitative projection analyses)
span.quote: The same method has been used in previous brain-wide quantitative analyses of projection patterns (Oh et al. 2014; Harris et al. 2019), and thus was used in this study for comparative analysis of inputs to/outputs from PPC.

span.label: builds-on → Zingg et al. 2017 (AAV1 transsynaptic anterograde tracing)
span.quote: Taking advantage of AAV1, which is a widely used anterograde tracer with transsynaptic potential (Zingg et al. 2017), in combination with reporter mouse line (Gt(ROSA)26Sortm9(CAG-tdTomato), Ai9), we selectively labeled the neuronal cell bodies that receive VISa inputs.

span.label: extends → the rat connectivity record in BAMS (Brain Architecture Management System)
span.quote: We also observed inputs from LGd, VPL, VPM and VAL in mice, which were not reported in rats (no reported data in BAMS).

span.label: contradicts → prior rat reports of a zona incerta (ZI) projection to VISrl
span.quote: It has been reported in rats that light projections from the ZI to the VISrl exist, however, we found no clear evidence of projections to the PPC (see Supplementary Figs 9 and 10k).

span.label: functional retinotopic mapping —contrasted-with→ architectonic definition
span.note: differs in: where each places the boundary: the functional maps were not clearly defined or did not match the architectonic one · strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: However, it has been reported that even with functional retinotopic mapping by intrinsic optical imaging, using voltage-sensitive dyes or Ca2+ responses, the boundaries of VISa and VISrl were not clearly defined or mismatched with the architectonic definition of the PPC

span.label: correlation
span.quote: The Pearson correlation of the top 25 projection targets between the selected and 13 other injections were very high, 0.97 ± 0.03, suggesting that any of these candidates could be selected as the representative.

span.label: standard deviation
span.quote: Individual values (P, R, I) were normalized (P, R, I) by using the mean and standard deviation of each structure

span.label: mean
span.quote: The mean projection strength was calculated for each target structure from 4–5 best injections for VISa (a and c) or VISrl (b and d) using a log10-transformed normalized projection volume.

span.label: The mouse posterior parietal cortex sends its heaviest cortical output to secondary motor cortex, primary visual cortex and the barrel field of primary somatosensory cortex.
span.quote: The PPC predominantly projected to secondary motor, primary visual, and the barrel field of the primary somatosensory cortex (MOs, VISp, and SSp-bfd; Figs 2 and 3).

span.label: PPC output to the thalamus is concentrated in three associative nuclei, LP, PO and LD.
span.quote: Strong PPC projections were found in the associative thalamic regions, LP, PO, and LD.

span.label: The heaviest inputs to the PPC come from ipsilateral secondary motor, auditory and visual cortex plus primary somatosensory cortex.
span.quote: The largest inputs arise from ipsilateral secondary cortical regions (motor, auditory, and visual) and the primary somatosensory region (Fig. 5).

span.label: Hypothalamic output of the PPC is essentially confined to the zona incerta, a connection not previously reported.
span.quote: Within the hypothalamus, moderate projections from the PPC appeared almost exclusively in the ZI, for both VISa and VISrl

span.label: What separates PPC from neighbouring visual cortex is that it gets more multimodal spatial input and less primary visual input.
span.quote: In summary, the enhanced multimodal spatial input and decreased primary visual input distinguishes the PPC from adjacent regions of the visual cortex.

span.label: The strongest reciprocal cortical partners of PPC are MOs, SSp-bfd, VISal, VISam and VISpm.
span.quote: In the cortex, MOs, SSp-bfd, VISal, VISam, and VISpm showed the greatest mutual connection, for which pairs both VISa and VISrl showed the projection strength above the threshold (Fig. 11a,b).

span.label: The strongest reciprocal thalamic partners of PPC are LP, PO, LD and PF.
span.quote: In the thalamus, LP, PO, LD, and PF were found to have the strongest reciprocal connections (Fig. 11c,d).

span.label: Neuromodulatory input to PPC is dominated by cholinergic fibres, with weaker serotonergic and histaminergic input.
span.quote: In summary, there was a distinct cholinergic input to the PPC, with much lighter serotonergic and histaminergic inputs to the PPC; patterns were similar in adjacent regions.

span.label: The posterior thalamic nucleus projects topographically, its dorsomedial neurons reaching VISa and its lateral neurons reaching VISrl.
span.quote: Dorsomedial PO neurons projected to VISa, whereas neurons in lateral portion of PO projected to VISrl almost exclusively (Fig. 9c,d).

span.label: Compared with rats, mice have lighter LD and LP projections to PPC but clear ventrobasal (VPL, VPM) and LGd input that rats were not reported to have.
span.quote: On the other hand, LD and LP projected more lightly to the PPC in mice than in rats, whereas the ventrobasal areas and the LGd appeared lightly, but clearly, in mice (Figs 5, 8, and 9).

span.label: The single largest mouse-rat discrepancy in PPC output is the infralimbic area, strongly innervated in rat and only trace-labelled in mouse.
span.quote: The greatest species differences in projection between mice and rats were noted in ILA.

span.label: Top-down cortical inputs from ILA and ACAd and higher-order thalamic input from VAL and PO terminate mainly in layer 1 of PPC.
span.quote: Top–down cortical inputs (ILA and ACAd) and high-order thalamic nuclei (VAL and PO) send their projections primarily to L1.

span.label: Overall the mouse PPC connectome closely resembles the rat's, with a minority of clear species differences.
span.quote: We found that the connectivity of the mouse PPC was remarkably similar to that of rats overall, while clear differences were also observed in some areas.

span.label: normalized projection volume
span.quote: 3. Normalized projection volume: Projection volume divided by injection volume.

span.label: injection volume
span.quote: 1. Injection volume: Sum of detected (as a signal, above threshold) pixels in mm3 within the injection site.

span.label: robustness of labeling (R)
span.quote: The robustness of labeling (R) was defined as the sum of projection volume in all targets in a given experiment.

span.label: inclusiveness of projection targets (I)
span.quote: The inclusiveness of projection targets (I) was calculated by counting target structures receiving at least 0.0001 of projection volume.

span.label: representative score (S)
span.quote: Then, the representative score (S) was defined by combining three values, with more weight on the injection accuracy (P), as follows:

span.label: reciprocality
span.quote: Then, the reciprocality was determined by the sum of projection strength divided by the difference between two projection strengths

span.label: bilaterality
span.quote: We then analyzed the bilaterality of the PPC to 43 cortical targets, which was determined by the ratio of the contralateral projections to the ipsilateral projections

span.label: virtual retrograde map
span.quote: true afferent inputs to the PPC were not directly characterized in this data, and thus retrograde connections were inferred by reanalysis of the connectivity data set

span.label: injection site within PPC (VISa versus VISrl coordinates)
span.term: injection site within PPC (VISa versus VISrl coordinates)
span.quote: Consequently, a total of three injection coordinates were used for each subregion of the PPC: 2.00, 2.10, and 2.20 mm posterior, 1.60, 1.80, and 2.00 mm lateral to the bregma for VISa

span.label: projection strength (normalized projection volume) to/from PPC
span.term: projection strength (normalized projection volume) to/from PPC
span.quote: The projection strength from these 214 structures to the PPC was calculated, normalized against each injection materials, and used for quantitative analysis of inputs to PPC

span.label: injection volume
span.quote: However, normalization by the injection volume is necessary when comparing multiple injections with various injection sizes, which vary in number of cells labeled and therefore the size of the potential projection.

span.label: image brightness and contrast
span.quote: All images were obtained at the same brightness/contrast level for comparison across regions, except for (n), where we increased the contrast to visualize a few yet clear anterograde labeling in ZI.

span.label: N = 2556 — number of published atlas injection experiments that passed the standard-labelling screen and entered the analysis
span.quote: and primary injection sites in the brain (excluding retinal injections) were considered for this analysis (N = 2556)

span.label: 214 — unique primary injection sites, one per brain structure, from which afferents to PPC were inferred
span.quote: This results in a total of 214 unique primary injection sites at an intermediate ontology level

span.label: 173 — representative injections selected for the noncortical (subcortical) structures
span.quote: The resulting 173 injections chosen for each noncortical area are robust, inclusive, and well-positioned to their targets (Fig. 1b).

span.label: 0.97 ± 0.03 — Pearson correlation of the top 25 projection targets between the chosen VISp representative injection and 13 alternative injections
span.quote: The Pearson correlation of the top 25 projection targets between the selected and 13 other injections were very high, 0.97 ± 0.03, suggesting that any of these candidates could be selected as the representative.

span.label: 0.1 for cortical and 0.05 for thalamic — normalized-projection-volume thresholds a connection had to exceed to be shown in the reciprocality analysis
span.quote: Only strong connections above threshold (0.1 for cortical and 0.05 for thalamic structures) are shown in a color scale (white/red).
